# Summary

In this report, we analyzed data within residents and directors, then compared the groups' (*i.e.* residents vs directors) answer selections, informing the difference that various factors can have on a resident's wellbeing and experience in their program, and if the directors have a different perception of what residents face during residency. Out of 81 total tests within the residents group, we found 5 to be significant at the $\alpha$ = 0.05 level. However, none of these were found to be significant after adjusting for multiple hypothesis testing via the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure to control false discovery rate (FDR). Out of 14 tests for directors, nothing was found to be significant either before or after adjustment for multiple hypotheses. When comparing across groups, we found 18 out of the 51 tests performed were significant after the BH adjustment. This means that at least 18 questions saw significant evidence of being answered differently for residents and directors. Results of all tests are reported in the significant findings section, and their significance before and after adjustment will be noted.

# Methods

We tested for associations between questions and differences in proportions across groups (residents vs directors) using Fisher exact tests. Low p-value's indicate significant results.

For questions with multiple parts, we split them into individual questions (e.g. 13a, 13b, 13c...) to see if there were specific responses that were influenced by the grouping variable in question, which was the role (being a resident/director) in the case of cross-comparison, or information like program, experience, etc.

Finally we present data visualizations to summarize the results. Interesting plots and findings were placed in the "significant findings" section with all plots appearing in are in the Appendix.

```{r packages, echo = FALSE, warnings = FALSE, message = FALSE}
library(likert)

library(gt)
set.seed(1)
```

# Cronbach's Alpha for burnout-related questions in residents

```{r alpha, echo = FALSE}
#exhaustion related questions + new comparisons 
exhaustion <- f_res_coalesced %>% select(PGY_level, gender, program_type, working_hours_per_week, call_days_per_month, quality_life, consider_quitting, feel_strained, feel_fatigued, feel_drained)

#depersonalization related questions + new comparisons 
depersonalization <- f_res_coalesced %>% select(PGY_level, gender, program_type, working_hours_per_week, call_days_per_month, quality_life, consider_quitting, feel_depersonalization, feel_carelessness, feel_callousness)

#personal accomplishment related questions + new comparisons 
accomplishment <- f_res_coalesced %>% select(PGY_level, gender, program_type, working_hours_per_week, call_days_per_month, quality_life, consider_quitting, feel_confidence, feel_exhilaration, feel_pos_influence)

# levels for this question
levels_feel <- c("Never","A few times in a year","Once per month or less","A few times in a month","A few times in a week","Once per week","Every day")

# creating likert scale values 
exhaustion <- exhaustion %>% mutate(across(.cols = c(feel_strained, feel_fatigued, feel_drained), .fns = ~  case_when(
  .x == "Never" ~ 1, 
  .x == "A few times in a year" ~ 2, 
  .x == "Once per month or less" ~ 3, 
  .x == "A few times in a month" ~ 4, 
  .x == "A few times in a week" ~ 5, 
  .x == "Once per week" ~ 6, 
  .x == "Every day" ~ 7
)))

depersonalization <- depersonalization %>% mutate(across(.cols = c(feel_depersonalization, feel_carelessness, feel_callousness), .fns = ~  case_when(
  .x == "Never" ~ 1, 
  .x == "A few times in a year" ~ 2, 
  .x == "Once per month or less" ~ 3, 
  .x == "A few times in a month" ~ 4, 
  .x == "A few times in a week" ~ 5, 
  .x == "Once per week" ~ 6, 
  .x == "Every day" ~ 7
)))

accomplishment <- accomplishment %>% mutate(across(.cols = c(feel_confidence, feel_pos_influence, feel_exhilaration), .fns = ~  case_when(
  .x == "Never" ~ 1, 
  .x == "A few times in a year" ~ 2, 
  .x == "Once per month or less" ~ 3, 
  .x == "A few times in a month" ~ 4, 
  .x == "A few times in a week" ~ 5, 
  .x == "Once per week" ~ 6, 
  .x == "Every day" ~ 7
)))

df_cronbach <- data.frame(Groups = c("Exhaustion", "Depersonalization", "Personal Accomplishment"), Alpha = c(
  as.numeric(psych::alpha(exhaustion[,c("feel_strained", "feel_fatigued", "feel_drained")] %>% drop_na())$total[1]),

as.numeric(psych::alpha(depersonalization[,c("feel_depersonalization", "feel_carelessness", "feel_callousness")] %>% drop_na())$total[1]),

as.numeric(psych::alpha(accomplishment[,c("feel_confidence", "feel_pos_influence", "feel_exhilaration")] %>% drop_na())$total[1])
))

df_cronbach <- df_cronbach %>% mutate(Significant = Alpha > 0.7)

```

# Item-total correlations for burnout-related subgroups 

Notable strength of correlation exists between feeling drained and strained (0.701), feeling callousness and depersonalization (0.674), feeling depersonalization and carelessness (0.599), and feeling callousness and carelessness (0.583). None of the personal accomplishment correlations were notably strong. These numbers were calculated exclusively from the residents response to burnout-related questions. 

```{r, echo = FALSE}
print("Item-total correlations Exhaustion Group")
cor(exhaustion %>% drop_na() %>% select(feel_strained, feel_fatigued, feel_drained))

print("Item-total correlations Depersonalization Group")
cor(depersonalization %>% drop_na() %>% select(feel_depersonalization, feel_carelessness, feel_callousness))

print("Item-total correlations Personal Accomplishment Group")
cor(accomplishment %>% drop_na() %>% select(feel_confidence, feel_pos_influence, feel_exhilaration))
```

# Composite Score Analysis

For the exhaustion and depersonalization groups, we created side-by-side box plots to visualize potential differences in distributions for each grouping variable in question. We then conducted a Kruskal-Wallis test to determine if there was statistical significance, and the p-values are recorded below. Notable box plots are included below, but all are reported in the appendix. 

```{r composite-score-analysis, echo = FALSE}

exhaustion <- exhaustion %>% mutate(score = feel_drained + feel_strained + feel_fatigued)

depersonalization <- depersonalization %>% mutate(score = feel_depersonalization + feel_carelessness + feel_callousness)

#"accomplishment" proved to be insignificant based on the cronbach's alpha value 

#accomplishment <- accomplishment %>% mutate(score = feel_confidence + feel_pos_influence + feel_exhilaration)

ggplot(exhaustion, aes(x = working_hours_per_week, y = score)) + geom_boxplot() + theme_bw()
ggplot(depersonalization, aes(x = working_hours_per_week, y = score)) + geom_boxplot() + theme_bw()

ggplot(exhaustion, aes(x = call_days_per_month, y = score)) + geom_boxplot() + theme_bw()
ggplot(depersonalization, aes(x = call_days_per_month, y = score)) + geom_boxplot() + theme_bw()

ggplot(exhaustion, aes(x = quality_life, y = score)) + geom_boxplot() + theme_bw()
ggplot(depersonalization, aes(x = quality_life, y = score)) + geom_boxplot() + theme_bw()

ggplot(exhaustion, aes(x = consider_quitting, y = score)) + geom_boxplot() + theme_bw()
ggplot(depersonalization, aes(x = consider_quitting, y = score)) + geom_boxplot() + theme_bw()

kruskal_df_exhaustion <- data.frame(Group = c(rep("Exhaustion", 7)), 
                         Score = c(rep("score", 7)), 
                         Comparison = c("PGY_level", "Gender", "Program Type", "Working Hours per Week", "Call Days per Month", "Quality of Life", "Consider Quitting"), 
                         P_values = c(
kruskal.test(score ~ PGY_level, data = exhaustion)$p.value,
kruskal.test(score ~ gender, data = exhaustion)$p.value,
kruskal.test(score ~ program_type, data = exhaustion)$p.value,
kruskal.test(score ~ working_hours_per_week, data = exhaustion)$p.value,
kruskal.test(score ~ call_days_per_month, data = exhaustion)$p.value,
kruskal.test(score ~ quality_life, data = exhaustion)$p.value,
kruskal.test(score ~ consider_quitting, data = exhaustion)$p.value))


kruskal_df_depersonalization <- data.frame(Group = c(rep("Depersonalization", 7)), 
                         Score = c(rep("score", 7)), 
                         Comparison = c("PGY_level", "Gender", "Program Type", "Working Hours per Week", "Call Days per Month", "Quality of Life", "Consider Quitting"), 
                         P_values = c(
kruskal.test(score ~ PGY_level, data = depersonalization)$p.value,
kruskal.test(score ~ gender, data = depersonalization)$p.value,
kruskal.test(score ~ program_type, data = depersonalization)$p.value,
kruskal.test(score ~ working_hours_per_week, data = depersonalization)$p.value,
kruskal.test(score ~ call_days_per_month, data = depersonalization)$p.value,
kruskal.test(score ~ quality_life, data = depersonalization)$p.value,
kruskal.test(score ~ consider_quitting, data = depersonalization)$p.value))

kruskal_df_exhaustion <- kruskal_df_exhaustion %>% mutate(Adj_P = round(p.adjust(P_values, method = "BH"), digits = 4)) %>% mutate(Significant = Adj_P <= 0.05)

kruskal_df_depersonalization <- kruskal_df_depersonalization %>% mutate(Adj_P = round(p.adjust(P_values, method = "BH"), digits = 4)) %>% mutate(Significant = Adj_P <= 0.05)

kruskal_df_exhaustion %>% select(Group, Score, Comparison, Adj_P, Significant) %>% arrange(Adj_P)

kruskal_df_depersonalization %>% select(Group, Score, Comparison, Adj_P, Significant) %>% arrange(Adj_P)
```

```{r validation-function, echo=FALSE}
# when trying to cross reference one question (question1) by another grouping variable (question2) 
validation <- function(question1, question2, data){
  df <- data %>%
    transmute(
      response1 = .data[[question1]],
      response2 = .data[[question2]]
    ) %>%
    drop_na()
  
  
  # comparison_res <- df %>%
  #   group_by(response1, response2) %>%
  #   summarize(counts = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  #   group_by(response2) %>%
  #   mutate(percent = counts / sum(counts) * 100) %>%
  #   ungroup()

  table_comparison <- table(df$response2, df$response1)
  
   if (nrow(table_comparison) < 2 | ncol(table_comparison) < 2) {
    return(tibble(
      Question1 = question1,
      Question2 = question2,
      P_value = NA_real_,
      Significant = NA,
      test = "insufficient categories"
    ))
  }

  test <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(table_comparison))
  
  if (mean(test$expected <= 5) < 0.8 | any(test$expected < 1)){
    fish_test <- fisher.test(table_comparison, simulate.p.value = TRUE)
    if (fish_test$p.value <= 0.05){
     significant <- TRUE
   }
   else {
      significant <- FALSE
   }
    return(c("question1", "question2", round(fish_test$p.value, digits = 4), significant,"fisher"))
  }
  else{
    if (test$p.value <= 0.05){
     significant <- TRUE
   }
   else {
      significant <- FALSE
   }
    }
  return(c("question1", "question2", round(test$p.value, digits = 4), significant, "chisq"))
}

```

# Likert Scale Analysis

We have now treated each factor-able variable on a likert scale and will conduct Kruskal-Wallis to determine if there exists conclusions to make on the directionality of the significance.

## Residents Likert Analysis

```{r likert-function, echo = FALSE}
likert_analysis <- function(factor_var, grouping_var, data){
  df <- data %>%
    transmute(
      factor_var = as.numeric(.data[[factor_var]]),
      grouping_var = .data[[grouping_var]]
    ) %>%
    drop_na()
  kw <- kruskal.test(factor_var ~ grouping_var, data = df)
  return(c("factor_var", "grouping_var", round(kw$p.value, digits = 4)))
}
```

```{r res-likert-results, echo = FALSE}
res_likert_results <- data.frame(
```

## Cross-comparison Likert Analysis

For the cross-comparison, we are not conducting the same test for each comparison. Since we're comparing the residents and directors' responses, both variables will be the same class (Likert or Categorical), so we will conduct the correct test accordingly: Fisher's Exact Test for categorical variables, and T-tests for Likert variables.

```{r cross-comp-function, echo = FALSE}
cross_validation_analysis <- function(question1, question2, data){
   df <- data %>%
    transmute(
      question1 = .data[[question1]],
      question2 = .data[[question2]]
    ) %>%
    drop_na()
   
   if (class(df$question1) == "character"){
     table_comparison <- table(df$question2, df$question1)
     fish_test <- fisher.test(table_comparison, simulate.p.value = TRUE)
     return(c("question1", "question2", round(fish_test$p.value, digits = 4), "fisher"))
   }
   else if (class(df$question1) == "factor"){
     df <- df %>%
    mutate(question1 = as.numeric(question1))
    t_test <- t.test(x = df$question1[df$question2 == "Director"], y = df$question1[df$question2 == "Resident"], alternative = "two.sided")
     return(c("question1", "question2", round(t_test$p.value, digits = 4), "t_test"))
   }
}
```

```{r cross-analysis, echo = FALSE}
cross_results <- data.frame(
  question1 = character(),
  question2 = character(),
  P_value = numeric(), 
  test = character()
)

for (i in seq_len(nrow(full_dic))) {
  cross_results[i, ] <- cross_validation_analysis(
    question1 = full_dic$common_qs[i],
    question2 = full_dic$role[i],
    data = full_named
  )
}

cross_results <- cross_results %>%
  mutate(
    Adj_P = round(p.adjust(P_value, method = "BH"), digits = 4),
    Sig_Adj = Adj_P <= 0.05,
    question1 = full_dic$common_qs, 
    question2 = full_dic$role
  ) %>% arrange(Adj_P)
cross_results %>% select(question1, question2, Sig_Adj, Adj_P, test)
```

```{r barplot-function, echo=FALSE}
stack_bar <- function(q_reference, q_group, data){
  bar_df <- data %>%
    group_by(.data[[q_reference]], .data[[q_group]]) %>%
    summarize(counts = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    drop_na() %>%
    group_by(.data[[q_group]]) %>%
    mutate(percent = counts / sum(counts) * 100) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  p <- ggplot(bar_df, aes(x = .data[[q_reference]], y = percent, fill = .data[[q_reference]])) +
    geom_col() +
    facet_wrap(vars(.data[[q_group]])) +
    labs(
      title = paste(q_reference, "vs", q_group, sep = " "),
      x = NULL,
      y = "Percent of responses"
    ) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
    )
  return(p)
}

```

# Significant Categorical Findings

## Residents Categorical Significance

The following relationships were found to be significant:

- Q13d/Q2: Treating patients as impersonal objects and PGY level

- Q13h/Q2: Not caring about what happens to certain patients and PGY level

- Q18/Q11: Working hours/week and desire to quit residency training

- Q16d/Q3: Experiencing sexual harassment and gender

- Q17/Q10: On call days/month and quality of life

```{r, echo = FALSE}
# plots_res_sig <- plots_res[c(25, 49, 79, 73, 75)]
# walk(plots_res_sig, print)
```

## Directors Categorical Significance

No tests in this group were found to be significant.

## Cross-Comparison Categorical Significance

Many questions were found to be significant between residents and directors, and below are all the questions that they responded significantly differently to:

- Q3: Gender

- Q12: Recreation hours per week

- Q13a/b/c/f: Feeling emotionally drained, fatigued, strained at work, not caring about what happens to patients

- Q14a/b: Negative impact on marriage, personal healthcare

- Q15a: Experienced discrimination based on gender

- Q19: Frequency of meeting with director

- Q20a/b/d: Frequency of discussing burnout, depression, quitting residency - notably, the only insignificant subquestion concerned suicidal thoughts

- Q21: Presence of standardized criteria for screening burnout & mental health

- Q22a/b/c: Satisfaction with how program manages burnout, depression, suicide

- Q26: Setting for screening (Anonymously vs Confidentially)
